Explore Arunachal Pradesh

About Arunachal Pradesh

Arunachal Pradesh is my dream destination because of its snow-capped peaks, hidden lakes and living tribal traditions. Few places in India still feel this untouched.

Arunachal Pradesh is the easternmost state of India, high in the Himalayas of the far Northeast. Its name is often translated as the Land of the Dawn-Lit Mountains. The state borders Bhutan, Tibet and Myanmar, and its forests, rivers, monasteries and valleys make it feel wonderfully remote.

  • Capital: Itanagar
  • Easternmost state
  • 83,743 km²
  • 25+ major tribes
  • First sunrise at Dong

Why Visit Arunachal Pradesh

Four reasons this state sits at the top of my travel list.

Mountain Adventures

Snowy passes like Sela, winding mountain roads and Himalayan views that feel a world away.

Himalayan Lakes

Clear high-altitude lakes such as Sangetsar, set among pine forests and quiet valleys.

Tribal Culture

More than 25 major tribes, each with its own language, festivals, music and handwoven textiles.

Local Flavours

Warm thukpa, momos, butter tea and bamboo-shoot dishes from kitchens high in the hills.

Top Destinations

Three places I would visit first, from a great monastery to a high pass and a green valley.

Tawang

Home to Tawang Monastery, the largest in India, founded in 1680–81 high above the Tawang Chu valley.

Explore

Sela Pass

A high Himalayan pass at about 13,700 feet. The Sela Tunnel, opened in 2024, helps keep the road to Tawang open.

Explore

Ziro Valley

A green plateau near 1,500 m, home to the Apatani people and their rice-fish farming, on UNESCO’s Tentative List.

Explore

Before You Go

A few things I want to get right before booking anything.

Best time

October to April for clear skies and snow, with rhododendrons in spring. The monsoon (June–September) can bring landslides.

Permit

Indian visitors from outside the state need an Inner Line Permit. Apply only on the official state government website and check the current rules first.

Getting there

Fly to Guwahati or Tezpur in Assam, or to Donyi Polo Airport near Itanagar, then continue by road. Mountain roads are slow, so allow extra time.

Festivals

Losar (February–March, Monpa), Dree (July, Apatani) and Solung (September, Adi) are the best times to meet local traditions.

Travel Plan

A five-day journey through western Arunachal, starting from Assam. Ziro is far to the east, so it is best as a separate trip.

DayPlaceActivity
Day 1BomdilaClimb into the hills from Assam, visit Bomdila Monastery and enjoy the mountain views.
Day 2Sela Pass to TawangStop in Dirang, cross Sela Pass at about 13,700 feet and drive on to Tawang.
Day 3TawangExplore Tawang Monastery, the largest in India, and its 8-metre gilded Buddha statue.
Day 4Sangetsar LakeVisit the high-altitude Sangetsar Lake and nearby Monpa villages.
Day 5ReturnDrive back through Sela Pass and Dirang towards Tezpur, with a bag full of memories.

My Travel Note

I would recommend Arunachal Pradesh to my friends because it offers breathtaking mountains, welcoming people and experiences you will not find anywhere else. It is a perfect destination for anyone who loves nature, culture and quiet roads.
